research_question: report 8822 reports dK_T(J=0.8) = -29.13 % but the same lattice carries a radial GCI of 7.1-8.1 %, so model error and discretisation error were not separable; this study builds >= 4-level ladders on five axes at three advance ratios and splits the deviation into a discretisation and a model term

criteria.statement: coverage: >= 4 levels on each axis, >= 12 (axis, J) cells, and K_T / 10 K_Q / eta_0 tabulated at every level
every level of every cell is physically admissible (K_T > 0, K_Q > 0, eta_0 <= momentum bound)
finest-level spanwise and azimuthal GCI of K_T <= 1 % (evidence-surface threshold of the mission)
finest-triplet observed order p >= 1.0 on the spanwise and azimuthal axes
the spanwise and azimuthal K_T ladders are monotone (no odd-even oscillation)
dK_T(J=0.8) is attributable to model error only when it lies outside the +/- 2 GCI band (GCI = RSS over the five axes)
POST-HOC sensitivity of G6: with the band restricted to the three discretisation axes (spanwise, azimuthal, chordwise), is dK_T(J=0.8) outside +/- 2 GCI?

evidence.why_post_hoc: G6 named the RSS over all five axes before the run; that band is dominated by the divergent wake-extent axis (see G8), so it mixes model-form error into the discretisation band. G6b narrows the band to the discretisation axes only. It was added after the first run and is labelled post-hoc so the predeclared verdict (G6) stays the one on the record.

criteria.statement: the discrete/model split closes: abs(d_disc + d_model - d_total) <= 1e-9 pp
the wake-extent axis converges: usable GCI, p >= 1.0 and GCI <= 1 % at every J
the kernel-regularisation axis converges: usable GCI, p >= 1.0 and GCI <= 1 % at every J

limitations: No blade-surface circumferential segmentation exists in a blade-fitted lifting-surface lattice, so the mission's "circumferential segments" axis is realised as the azimuthal segmentation of the helical wake (`wake_steps`), the only azimuthal discretisation the model has. Recorded as a declared substitution, not silently renamed.

The solver is direct-dense with no fixed-point relaxation coefficient; the mission's "relaxation factor" axis is therefore realised as the van Garrel vortex-core desingularisation ratio, the only regularisation parameter. Its fine end (0.05) sits on the code's floor `core = max(core_ratio * segment, 0.5 * span)`, so the axis saturates there and the reported `p` describes the approach to that floor, not to an unregularised kernel.

The reported GCI is a discretisation band around the *lattice* solution, not an uncertainty on the anchor: the transcribed Table 2 values themselves carry measurement/reading uncertainty that this artefact does not quantify (see the provenance depth field of the anchor block).

The observed order of the spanwise ladder is negative at every J once the triplet is taken on the fine side (p = -1.520, -1.595, -1.565), while the coarse-side triplet of the same four-level ladder reports p = 2.878, 3.016, 3.050. The lattice is therefore not in the asymptotic range and no GCI from it is a bound; the numbers are reported as measured instead of being fitted to a p >= 1 expectation.
Only J = 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0 are ladders; the remaining anchor points keep the single-density evidence of the sweep study (docs/m7485_kp505_openwater_bem.md).
